question.leadin: Answer the following about Douglas MacArthur.
question.text: Truman dismissed Douglas MacArthur and replaced him with Matthew Ridgway during this war. MacArthur led a surprise amphibious landing at Incheon (IN-chon) during this war.
question.clue: Task Force Faith was disbanded after losing a battle on the east side of the Chosin Reservoir in this war, but U.S. marines to the south fought out of a Chinese encirclement.

swap.leadin: Operation Paul Bunyan involved the use of overwhelming military force to chop down a tree in this area.
swap.text: Name this area which separates North and South Korea from each other. The Joint Security Area within this zone is used for diplomatic meetings.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a certain class of warship.
question.text: An earlier example of an ironclad warship was this type of ship developed by Admiral Yi Sun-sin to resist a 16th century Japanese invasion of Korea. Named for the shape of the animal on its bow, these ships boasted cannons and a hull covered in spikes.
question.clue: Soldiers from Ming China helped defend Korea from Japanese invasion at the end of the 16th century. During that conflict, Korean Admiral Yi utilized these crazy awesome vessels which received their name from the appearance caused by their armored decks.

swap.leadin: Name these places identified with the Korean War.
swap.text: This village in the DMZ was the location of the peace talks between the two sides, and talks still go on just outside this village.
swap.clue: This village which hosted a more famous conference that led to the armistice between United Nations forces and communists in 1953 during the Korean War.

question.leadin: According to the Samguk sagi, this kingdom was founded by Jumong, whose wife headed south to found the Baekje kingdom.
question.text: Name this northernmost of the 3 kingdoms of the peninsula which now bears its name, along with Baekje and Silla. At its peak part of this kingdom extended into Manchuria and Siberia.
question.clue: Some of the best-preserved art of this kingdom survives in the tomb of Dong Shou at a complex at Anak.

swap.leadin: This event transformed one country's economy from one of the poorest in the world to one of the largest in the region.
swap.text: Name this event during which the emergence of Chaebol conglomerates helped spur the rapid modernization and economic growth of an Asian country.

question.text: During the war, U.N. pilots also referred to the northwest of Korea as "[these planes] Alley," since Americans F-86 Sabres often encountered Soviet aircraft there.
question.clue: During the war, the northwest of North Korea gained this nickname from UN forces, due to the presence of Soviet fighter planes here. Along the Yalu River, this region was the site of many dogfights.

swap.leadin: Operation Paul Bunyan took place in this area as a result of an axe murder incident.
swap.text: Name this heavily fortified strip of land created in July 1953. An armistice was signed in Panmunjom ["pan-moon-jum"], a village within this area.
swap.answerHtml: Demilitarized Zone (or DMZ; prompt on Joint Security Area or JSA; prompt on North Korea–South Korea border, but do NOT REVEAL this)
swap.clue: This no-man's-land along the 38th parallel. It was created in a July 1953 armistice.

question.leadin: June 25 will mark the 50th anniversary of the start of the Korean War. Answer these questions on the conflict.
question.text: When the U.N. approved the reunification of Korea as a military goal, the Chinese army entered to support the North Koreans, crossing this river.
question.clue: The Friendship Bridge is the only remaining bridge over this river and connects the cities of Dandong and Sinujiu.

swap.text: China's civil service exam was imitated by the gwageo, an exam popular during this empire. Chogye Buddhism flourished in this kingdom, which was founded by Taejo and fought a series of wars against the Khitans.
swap.clue: Twenty-nine women from hojeok ("HO-juck") families were married to this dynasty's founder, Wang Geon ("gun").

question.text: A period of this name in earlier Korean history involved states like Baekje ("pek-cheh") and Silla. Another period of this name in China included conflicts between Zhuge Liang ("JOO-guh LYONG") and Cao Cao ("tsao tsao").
question.clue: The "Later" part of a period with this name was dominated by a Unified Silla that conquered Goguryeo.

swap.leadin: This country was the site of political protests after police shot protesters at Masan Harbor.
swap.text: Name this country whose April Revolution forced its first president to resign. A president of this country who took power in a coup ordered the Gwangju Massacre in 1980.
swap.clue: Nearly 300 high school students drowned on a ferry boat in this country in 2014.

question.leadin: These campaigns are sometimes called the "Ceramic Wars" because potters were kidnapped and moved to Arita, where they developed one country's porcelain industry.
question.text: Name these campaigns during which soldiers reportedly cut off the noses of their victims as trophies because heads were too unwieldy to haul around.
question.answerHtml: Japanese invasions of Korea [accept Hideyoshi’s invasions of Korea; accept Imjin Wars]
question.clue: That one of these events eventually ended at the Battle of Noryang.

swap.text: Members of this Joseon noble, scholarly class were expected to be knowledgeable in the Confucian classics. To enter this class, one had to perform well on the gwageo civil service exam.
swap.clue: Seowon [suh-wun] were private schools constructed for the education of this class, which was wealthier than the sangmin [sahng-meen]. A genealogy book called a jokbo [choke-boh] could be used to prove one's membership in this Korean class.

question.text: In the Joseon period, this social group, who have been categorised as enslaved or serfs, were around 40% of the population in the 17th century. Unlike in the Goryeo period, most of this class were privately owned rather than publicly.

swap.leadin: This politician initiated a campaign to collect gold from his country's citizens to repay its debts to the IMF.
swap.text: Name this politician who steered his country through the 1997 Asian financial crisis. This politician's Sunshine Policy earned him the 2000 Nobel Peace Prize.
swap.clue: Pope John Paul II interceded to save this man from being executed after the Gwangju People's Uprising.

question.leadin: Guerrillas in this uprising set up bases in the caves around Hallasan, an extinct volcano where remains of victims can still be found, and attacked paramilitary troops of the Northwest Youth League.
question.text: Name this massacre that lasted over a year from April 1948 to 1949, in a nation being occupied under Operation Blacklist Forty.

swap.text: In 935, General Wang Kon overthrew the Silla Kingdom to establish this successor state, which ruled the peninsula until 1392 and produced valuable celadon ceramics.

question.leadin: Now located at the National Library of France, it was composed by the Buddhist monk Baegun around 1372 AD, and published by his students Seoksan and Daldam. FTPE.
question.text: Name this two-volume Korean anthology of Zen Buddhist teachings which is the oldest existing metal-plate printed book.

swap.text: Kim first gave guidance tours during a 1950s industrial program named for this legendarily fast creature. Under Kim Jong Un, workers have been encouraged to move with the speed of a 10-times-faster version of this creature, which also names a huge steel complex in Nampo.
swap.answerHtml: Chollima [or Cheollima; accept Chollima Movement or Chollima Steel Complex; accept qiānlǐmǎ; accept Mallima; accept “Mallima Speed”]
